title: Configurable retention rules and evidence export for LLM traffic
creator: Maya Alvarez
description:
Background: Customers operating in regulated industries require fine-grained control over how long different types of inference data are retained (prompts, model responses, request/response metadata, metrics) and a simple way to produce auditable evidence that retention settings are being enforced. Current platform retention is global and coarse; this ticket defines product requirements for per-tenant and per-route retention rules, residency-aligned storage targets, and an automated evidence/export pipeline for compliance auditors.

Goals:
- Provide a console and API for configuring retention policies at org, workspace, and route levels with presets (e.g., 30d/90d/1y/never) and custom TTLs.
- Allow policy scoping by data type: prompts, responses, request logs (headers/metadata), and aggregated metrics.
- Support data residency enforcement: map retention buckets to storage regions (US/EU/APAC) and surface validation warnings.
- Build an evidence export job that bundles immutable metadata and signed manifests for a given time window, usable for regulator audits.
- Provide a retention simulator to estimate storage, cost, and expected deletion volumes before applying policies.

Out of scope: per-model token-level redaction, end-user PII detection/remediation (separate privacy product).

Motivation: This unlocks sales to regulated customers and reduces manual support work for retention evidence requests.
acceptance_criteria: Console: 'Retention policies' page where admins can create policies and assign them to workspace(s) or routes
API: CRUD endpoints for retention policies with schema validation and policy assignment endpoints
Policy granularity: support separate TTLs for: prompts, responses, request_logs, metrics as explicit fields
Residency mapping: each policy can select a storage region; requests are validated against customer's residency constraints
Enforcement: background retention worker deletes expired items within SLA (deletion visibility within 24h of TTL expiration) and writes deletion audit events
Evidence export: scheduled and on-demand exports produce a signed bundle (manifest + hash list) covering a time window and list of policies applied
Simulator: UI shows estimated monthly storage and cost delta for a given policy before saving
Docs & Support: Playbook and API docs for evidence export and retention verification published
Performance: retention enforcement and evidence export do not increase median request latency by >5%
Telemetry: console shows per-policy counts (active objects, expected deletions, last enforcement run).

risks: Incorrect deletion could cause data loss and legal exposure — require strong safety nets and multi-step deletion with immutable audit manifest
Export bundles may expose sensitive content — must be encrypted and access-controlled via KMS/HSM
Cost estimation may be inaccurate for high-cardinality workloads — simulator should include conservative error bounds
Performance: bulk deletion and export operations could impact storage IO — schedule off-peak and rate-limit jobs
Operational: retrofitting retention into existing storage layer requires cross-team coordination and migration plan
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (spec + RFC): Policy schema and enforcement contract agreed (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (internal alpha): Implement retention worker + console UI, test on canary internal orgs (3 weeks)
Phase 2 (pilot): Enable for 3 pilot customers paying attention to residency mapping and export testing (4 weeks)
Phase 3 (gradual rollout): Opt-in for customers, collect feedback, add cost simulator improvements (4 weeks)
Phase 4 (default enablement): Offer as GA with migration tooling and announcement (2 weeks)
